name: Patrice O'Neal
note: STAGE PERSONA graph for the 'Why is X Funny?' video series. Graph-only. 0 sets measured — all hypothesis. Public persona only, no biography.

identity.deal: Truth-telling bully who loved the room so much he'd fight it until it told the truth back.
identity.premise: A man who treated every social lie as an enemy, and the audience as a suspect he was interrogating with love.
identity.awareness_note: Fully aware the bully is a love language; the craft is the interrogation.

philosophy.ontology: Social life is a series of lies everyone agrees to tell.
philosophy.epistemology: If the room is uncomfortable, you're over the target.
philosophy.axiology: The truth is a form of love, even when it doesn't feel like it.
philosophy.causality: One good interrogation can collapse a whole room's self-image.
philosophy.agency: Anyone can be a bully; almost nobody bullies toward the truth.

dramatic_core.fear: being the one who lied — he'd turn on himself first
dramatic_core.need: to be loved for the truth, not despite it
dramatic_core.self_model: a man holding a mirror up to the room and not letting go
blind_spots: the bully can become a cage
the truth can lose the room

identity.misinterpretation_rule: Treats every social lie as a challenge, then follows the lie until the room confesses.
contradictions: the bully with the biggest heart
the truth-teller who loved the lie-tellers
the man who fought the room and won it

status_model.desired_status: the one who tells the truth
status_model.felt_status: a man permanently at war with the room he loves

expression.emotional_restraint: low — the love is in the fight
tells: the laugh that is also a cry

profile.pace: accelerating interrogation, hard stop on the kill

threads: the social lie as an enemy
the bully as a love language
the truth as a form of care
the interrogation as a comic form
identity.style_thesis: Truth-bully engine: loved the room so much he'd fight it until it told the truth back. The bully is a love language; the interrogation is the craft. The truth is a form of love, even when it doesn't feel like it.

set_queue.note: For 'Why is X Funny?' — ingest 1-2 signature-era sets, ASR + word-timed.

timing_profile.doctrine_hypothesis: Accelerating interrogation, hard stop on the kill. The bully voice is the timing device — the room braces, then the tender turn arrives. The laugh that is also a cry is the tell.

internal.cite: Attardo & Raskin — General Theory of Verbal Humor
internal.claim: Joke = {SO, LM, SI, TA, NS, LA}. Technique and Narrative Strategy shape how the mechanism is staged.

internal.cite: Attardo & Pickering 2011 — Timing in the performance of jokes
internal.claim: Punch lines preceded by substantial pauses (0.6-0.8s+); timing = pause distribution + speech rate.

internal.cite: arxiv 2605.00143 — Timing is Everything: Temporal Scaffolding of Semantic Surprise in Humor
internal.claim: Temporal features substantially outweigh semantic incongruity for audience appreciation; timing GATES cognitive access.
Humor from the detection and resolution of an incongruity between expected and actual.
Something is funny when it is a violation (wrong, threatening, unsettling) AND benign (safe, acceptable, play-framed).

internal.cite: Roger & Duffy / status theory of humor
internal.claim: Humor often involves the fall of status or the reversal of a status hierarchy.
Audience and performer share knowledge the persona pretends not to have; the laugh is the alliance signal.

internal.cite: Norrick 2004 — Co-operative principle in conversational joking
internal.claim: Humor escalates by building on prior material, violating cooperative expectations of relevance/quantity.
